data.narrative:
StoreDot, a Series E-stage frontier technology company in Climate & Energy, has raised $206.5M to date. The valuation landscape includes a narrow peer set of one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private competitors in the sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation approach for this analysis. Using total capital raised of $206M as a valuation proxy, a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E advancement yields an implied valuation of $289M. This method applies when peer-set specificity is constrained. Peer-median analysis is not applicable here: while eight same-sector peers exist, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded insufficient datapoints (fewer than three required observations). A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable methodological noise.

The triangulated valuation range supported by this analysis spans $246M (low) to $332M (high), with a median of $289M. This range reflects a ±15% confidence interval around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties center on the adequacy of the $206M raised proxy as a valuation anchor in an illiquid sector, and the absence of sufficiently similar peer transactions to validate or adjust the 1.4x multiplier. Investors should weight this valuation against private market transaction evidence and founder exit expectations.
